questions.q:
What is one primary function of a Gram Panchayat regarding village infrastructure?
(Recall)
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat maintains village roads and drains. A student who mentions "laws for the whole country" is confusing the national government with local government.

questions.q:
Why is it better for a village to have its own Panchayat instead of waiting for the state government to fix every small issue?
(Understand)
questions.a: The Panchayat is closer to the people and understands specific local needs faster. A student who says "they have more money than the state" is incorrect; they are just more accessible and specialized in local matters.

questions.q:
If a village wants to start a new sanitation campaign to keep the streets clean, which local body is responsible for implementing it?
(Apply)
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat is responsible. If the student names the "police" or "District Collector," they fail to recognize that development schemes are the mandate of the elected local council.

questions.q:
How do the roles of a Gram Panchayat differ from the roles of a higher-level government (like the State or Central government)?
(Analyze)
questions.a: Local government focuses on immediate daily needs like water and street lights, while higher levels handle broad policy, national defense, and state-wide laws. A student failing this sees no difference between the scale of governance.

questions.q:
Is it fair to expect the Gram Panchayat to solve every single problem in a village, such as a major highway construction? Why or why not?
(Evaluate)
questions.a: No, because the Panchayat has limited resources and jurisdiction; major highways involve state and central planning. A student who says "yes" ignores the reality of administrative limits and resource allocation.

questions.q:
If you were the Sarpanch of a village with no library, what steps would you take to provide one for the children?
(Create)
questions.a: The student should suggest: 1) Proposing the idea at a Gram Sabha meeting, 2) Checking available budget, 3) Seeking community support/space, 4) Implementing the plan. A poor answer lacks the democratic process of consulting the community.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The functions of local ______ are the specific tasks performed by elected village and urban councils to provide essential services and improve daily life for residents.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you wake up and find the ______ hand pump is broken and the main road is blocked by mud after a heavy rain—who fixes it?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to categorize at least three specific tasks of a Gram Panchayat and explain why these tasks are necessary for the village community.
